assumptions: A test-adequacy mechanism, NOT a proof of semantic correctness. The mutation-testing literature is explicit that a mutant set is not a completeness argument — equivalent mutants and missing fault classes remain real limits — and this rule inherits that limit.
The rule is stated over a fault model of IMPLEMENTATIONS. GPT-5.6’s M7 (⊤-only controls) mutates the SUITE instead, and that is a different object which this formulation does not cover.
attrs.evidence: GPT-5.6’s answer to R7.4 §8.2, which asked whether there is a general rule beyond `test at singletons` after R7.3’s control seeded ⊤ — the one value where identity and ⊤ agree. THE RULING: a singleton was never magical, it was a DISTINGUISHING INPUT for one particular mutant, and the general form is mutation adequacy — ∀ m ∈ M, m ≢ S ⇒ ∃ c ∈ C : S(c) ≠ m(c). R7.4’s own candidate (`seed where the correct and most likely wrong implementations disagree`) was close and required naming the wrong implementation with no way to make that mechanical; a REGISTERED fault model is exactly that mechanism. AND THE SHARPER HALF: when the semantic domain is finite, do not hand-pick a discriminating control at all — enumerate the domain and prove the executable transformer has the law. `Test at join-irreducibles` is explicitly NOT the rule adopted, because singletons alone cannot see the non-additive synergy this same algebra needs: T({correctness}) and T({confidentiality}) do not determine T({correctness, confidentiality}).
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6, on ROUND7_4_MOSAIC_BRIEF.md §8.2, citing the mutation-testing literature (SRC-MUTATION-ADEQUACY) for mutants, kills and non-equivalence.

readjudicated.method: redeclared_by_target — a declared design invariant is adopted deliberately, not inherited
readjudicated.note: The source-lane status is recorded in imported_from.source_status as provenance. This field records that the TARGET lane re-established it; the two are separate facts and the gate reads this one.

attrs.review_focus: The part worth attacking is the KILL CRITERION rather than the rule. `Some check went red` is unsound: a mutant that promotes an edge to operational DELETES that edge’s check instead of failing it. §3 demonstrates it — M3 fails zero battery rows and is killed only because a row VANISHED.
attrs.statement: A control suite for a semantic law must be evaluated against a declared fault model. For every non-equivalent registered mutant m, at least one control must produce a different observable result under m than under the reference semantics.
